emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(h->surplus_huge_pages)]) from thread_a (the counter read driving the reservation-restore decision must not race a concurrent update)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@alloc_surplus_hugetlb_folio:2272 = WRITE(h->surplus_huge_pages++) by thread_b under hugetlb_lock
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_a reads the counter while holding only the page-table lock (ptl), NOT hugetlb_lock; thread_b updates it under hugetlb_lock -> the two accesses share no common lock (ptl does not protect this hstate counter) -> no serialize establishes ρ
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent write held under a different lock -> data race; the racy value influences a reservation-restore decision

fix_maps_to: patch takes spin_lock_irq(&hugetlb_lock) around the surplus_huge_pages read in __unmap_hugepage_range (dropping ptl first) -> adds serialize(hugetlb_lock, [read]) on the reader side -> reader and writer now share the same lock -> establishes ρ. (The same patch also re-inits adjust_reservation per loop iteration, a single-thread logic fix, not the race.)
recall_risk_notes: Reader is NOT lock-free -- it holds ptl, the WRONG lock. Recall depends on (a) keeping candidate lock hugetlb_lock for the writer and (b) the LLM REJECTING ptl as protecting this field (ptl guards PTEs, not the hstate counter) -- the 'reject candidate lock' decision is the weakest link (WF3). If static/LLM treat 'reader holds a lock' as protected, the race is suppressed (FN). Object identity (h = hstate_vma(vma)) is clean.
